rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a lecture header reading as a bare instruction/label where the room needs a landed claim. Re-checked all six `##` headers against the current body this session. 'Passing is not proof', 'The judge needs calibrating against your own judgement', 'Gates decay', 'One session is a sample' are unambiguous declarative claims (subject + verb). Closest candidate for a violation: 'Change on recurrence, not on noise' — 'Change' can be misread as a bare imperative verb (an exercise-shaped instruction) rather than an elliptical noun-subject claim. Reading it against the header's own bullets settles it: none of the three bullets is a direct command paired to the header (line 34 is a definition of tampering, line 35 opens with its own internal imperative 'React on recurrence' distinct from the header, line 36 is a warning about a trap) — the header functions as the label for the law being taught, not an instruction to execute, parallel in construction to 'Gates decay' (bare noun + verb, no object). The maintainer's 'Laws carried' note (maintainer block) files this heading among the deck's five named laws ('don't-tamper (change on recurrence)'), same class as Goodhart's law and one-run-is-a-sample — documented intent supports the declarative reading. 'The delegation frontier' is a catalogue entry naming its subject, matching this rule's own cleared examples ('Ralph', 'The numbers') — explicit not-a-violation. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a bullet that reads as rigour but adds nothing beyond what the slide already holds. Scanned all 20 body bullets against the three classes this session. (a) doctrine restatement: none found — each of the five laws states its content once per slide, no law re-announced after it already did its work (e.g. slide 1's four bullets progress gate→check→countermoves→independence-property, no bullet repeats an earlier one's content). (b) self-referential design commentary: none — body stays first-order about gates, judges, and delegation throughout; no line tells the reader they are inside a pedagogy. (c) aphorism kicker restating the header or a `**The point:**` line: checked every chunk's final bullet as highest-risk position — line 9 ('A same-window double-check has none of it; the second read inherits the first one's framing') introduces the shared-framing mechanism, new content, not a restatement of 'Passing is not proof'; line 47's closing imperative 'Retire what the next model outgrows, add what it needs' is the payoff of the bitter-lesson point stated in the same bullet, not a koan restating 'The delegation frontier'. Two prior instances of exactly this pattern are confirmed already cut from this file: the maintainer block (L170) dates a class-(c) aphorism-kicker cut ('A gate is one more claim in the system…') to 2026-08-25 and names this rule by number; `grep -n 'one more claim in the system' curriculum/lectures/the-gate-is-a-claim.md` → exit 1, zero hits this session, confirming it stayed cut.
